Quitline Privacy Policy

Effective October 8, 2026 · Last updated October 8, 2026

The short version. Your quit journey (habits, check-ins, journal, slips, reasons) is stored on your iPhone. There is no account and we run no server, so we never have your data. You can sync it through your own iCloud if you choose. Purchases go through Apple. The free version shows ads; the ad companies collect some device data to show them, never your health or journal data, and Pro removes ads entirely.

Who we are

Quitline is made by an independent developer ("we", "us"). This policy covers the Quitline iPhone app, its widgets, Live Activities and Siri/Shortcuts actions. Quitline is an independent self-help app and is not affiliated with any government or public "quitline" service. Questions: SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD.

Your data stays on your device

Everything you enter in Quitline is stored in the app's private storage on your iPhone:

  • the habits you're quitting or cutting down, quit dates, cost and amount per day, and triggers;
  • slips, urges, puff counts, taper plans, milestones and pledges;
  • daily check-ins (mood, cravings, confidence) and journal entries;
  • your reasons, including any photos you attach (copied into the app from the photo picker; Quitline does not get access to the rest of your library);
  • a support person's name and phone number, if you add one;
  • lesson progress and settings (reminder times, app lock, theme).

We have no server for this data and cannot see it. Patterns such as your hardest hours are calculated on your iPhone. It is included in your own device backups (iCloud Backup or a computer backup), which Apple and you control.

Optional iCloud sync

Where the app offers it, you can turn on iCloud sync in Quitline Settings to keep your data in step across your own devices. It is off unless you turn it on. When on, your Quitline data is stored in the private iCloud database of your Apple ID using Apple's CloudKit. Only your devices signed in to that Apple ID can read it; we cannot access it. Apple's handling of iCloud data is covered by the Apple Privacy Policy and the iCloud terms. You can turn sync off at any time; see deleting your data for removing the iCloud copy.

Things you choose to share

Quitline never sends anything on its own. These features only share what you choose, through iOS's own share sheet, Messages or Phone app:

  • Partner codes: a short code with your streak numbers (and an "I'm struggling" note or habit name only if you include them), sent by you to someone you choose. It never includes your journal.
  • Share cards: an image of a milestone you choose to share (habit name hidden by default).
  • Call or text my person and crisis lines: open the Phone or Messages app, or a helpline website. Those services have their own privacy practices.
  • Export: a file of all your data, saved or sent wherever you choose. Keep it somewhere safe; it contains your personal journal.

Permissions

  • Notifications (optional): check-in reminders, milestones and, if you turn them on, heads-ups before your typical high-risk times. All are scheduled locally on your iPhone; no notification server is used.
  • Face ID / Touch ID / passcode (optional app lock): handled entirely by iOS. Quitline only learns whether unlocking succeeded; it never receives biometric data.
  • Photos: only the photos you pick for your reasons, through Apple's photo picker.
  • App Tracking Transparency (free version): see Advertising.

Widgets and Live Activities show neutral text such as "Day 42", never what you're quitting, and you can hide Quitline's content in the app switcher.

Network connections

Quitline works offline. It connects to the internet only for: Apple's App Store (prices, purchases, restores, subscription status); iCloud sync, if you turn it on (through Apple); links you tap, such as helpline websites; and ads in the free version. You can check this yourself in iOS's App Privacy Report (Settings > Privacy & Security > App Privacy Report).

Purchases and subscriptions

Quitline Pro is sold through Apple's App Store using StoreKit. Apple handles the payment, your payment details, your Apple ID and your billing address. We never see your name, email address or payment information. The app only receives a signed confirmation from Apple saying which product is active (for example, "Yearly, renews on a date" or "Lifetime") so it can unlock Pro and switch off ads. That check happens on your device. Apple's handling of purchase data is covered by Apple's Privacy Policy.

App Store Connect gives us aggregated, non-identifying sales reports (for example, how many trials started in a country). Apple does not give us your identity.

Advertising in the free version

The free version of Quitline shows ads. Buying Quitline Pro (a subscription or the lifetime purchase) removes all ads, and the ad SDK then stops requesting ads.

Ads are delivered by AppLovin MAX, an ad mediation SDK built into the app. MAX may fill an ad slot from AppLovin itself or from other ad networks it mediates, such as Google AdMob. These companies, not us, receive and process the data described below. We do not receive it in a form that identifies you; we only see aggregated reports such as how many ads were shown and how much they earned.

What the ad SDKs may collect

DataWhenUsed for
Advertising identifier (IDFA)Only if you tap "Allow" on Apple's App Tracking Transparency prompt. If you choose "Ask App Not to Track", iOS gives the SDK an all-zeros identifier instead.Personalized ads, measuring ads across apps (tracking)
Identifier for Vendor (IDFV) and SDK-generated IDsWhenever an ad is requestedFrequency capping, fraud prevention, reporting; not linked across companies' apps without your permission
IP address and approximate (coarse) location derived from itWhenever an ad is requestedDelivering ads, picking the right language/region, legal compliance (for example, privacy rules by region), fraud prevention
Device and app information: device model, iOS version, language, time zone, screen size, network type, carrier, app name and versionWhenever an ad is requestedShowing ads that fit your device, troubleshooting, fraud prevention
Ad interaction data: which ads were shown, taps, video completions, rewarded-ad completionsWhen you see or interact with an adAd delivery, measurement, billing between ad companies, rewarding you for a rewarded ad
Ad SDK diagnostics (crash and performance data about the ad SDK)If the ad SDK has a problemKeeping the ad SDK working

Ad SDKs never get access to your habits, quit dates, check-ins, moods, cravings, slips, journal, reasons, photos, support contacts or any other health and wellness information you enter. That information stays on your device (and in your own iCloud, if you turn on sync), is never shared with ad partners, and is never used to choose which ads you see. As with any app that shows ads, an ad request does tell the ad network which app it came from (Quitline). Ads never appear on the panic, breathing, urge-surfing or crisis-help screens.

The app does not request precise location for ads and does not give ad SDKs access to your contacts, camera, microphone or Health data.

Your ad choices

  • App Tracking Transparency (all users). The first time ads might be personalized, the app explains why and then shows Apple's prompt. Choose "Ask App Not to Track" and the ad SDKs cannot use your IDFA or track you across other companies' apps and websites; you will still see ads, but they are non-personalized or based on the content of the app. You can change this at any time in iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking (per app, or turn off "Allow Apps to Request to Track" for every app).
  • In-app consent manager (EEA, UK, Switzerland and US states with privacy laws). Where the law requires it, a consent screen (Google's User Messaging Platform, shown through AppLovin MAX) asks before any data is used for personalized ads, and lets you accept, reject or pick partners and purposes. You can reopen it at any time from Quitline Settings > Ad Privacy Choices to change or withdraw your consent, or to opt out of the "sale" or "sharing" of personal information for targeted advertising.
  • Remove ads entirely by buying Quitline Pro. A subscription or lifetime purchase turns off all ads.
  • Limit ad personalization at the partner. Google: My Ad Center.

Ad partners and their privacy policies

  • AppLovin (MAX mediation and AppLovin ads): applovin.com/privacy
  • Google AdMob: Google Privacy Policy and How Google uses information from apps that use its services

We may add or remove mediated ad networks over time. When we add one, we will list it here and update the changelog at the bottom of this page. The full, current list of partners and purposes is also shown in the consent screen where that screen applies.

We ask our ad partners to block ads for alcohol, tobacco and vaping products, and gambling, where their controls allow it. If you ever see an ad like that in Quitline, please tell us at SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD.

Health information

Information about smoking, vaping, drinking, gambling, mood and cravings can be sensitive. That is why it never leaves your control: it stays on your device (or your own iCloud), it is not shared with ad partners or anyone else, and it is not used for advertising, profiling or research. Quitline does not read from or write to Apple Health. We do not collect "consumer health data" as defined by laws such as Washington's My Health My Data Act.

What we never do

  • No account, sign-in or email address needed.
  • No server holding your journey, and no analytics or crash-reporting SDKs of our own. (Ad SDKs may report their own diagnostics, as described above.)
  • We never sell your data and never use your habit or journal data for advertising.

Data retention

  • On-device data is kept until you delete it (individual entries, Delete everything, or deleting the app). We keep no copy.
  • iCloud sync data (if you turned it on) stays in your iCloud until you delete it.
  • Ad data is retained by AppLovin, Google and other ad partners according to their policies linked above.
  • Purchase records are kept by Apple under Apple's policies.
  • Support emails are kept only as long as needed to help you and keep a record of the conversation, then deleted, normally within 24 months. Ask us to delete them sooner at any time.

Exporting and deleting your data

  • Export: Quitline Me > Settings > Your data > Export creates a file with everything you've entered.
  • Delete everything: Me > Settings > Your data > Delete everything (type DELETE to confirm). This erases all your Quitline data, scheduled reminders and widget content on this device, and, with iCloud sync on, from your iCloud too.
  • iCloud copy: you can also remove it in iOS Settings > [your name] > iCloud > Manage Account Storage (select Quitline and delete its data, where listed).
  • Deleting the app removes its on-device data. It does not cancel a subscription.
  • Ad data: use your ad choices or contact the ad partner; email us and we'll help.

Your privacy rights

Because Quitline has no account and no server, we do not hold a profile about you. Your app data is on your device, where you can view, export (where the app offers it) and delete it yourself. For data the ad partners collect, you can use the choices above or contact the partner directly. Whatever your location, you can email us and we will help.

EEA, UK and Switzerland (GDPR / UK GDPR)

  • Who is responsible. We, the developer of Quitline, are the controller for the limited personal data we handle (for example, emails you send us, and the decision to integrate ad SDKs). AppLovin, Google and other ad partners act as independent controllers for the data they collect to deliver and measure ads.
  • Legal bases. Personalized ads and the access to device identifiers they need: your consent, collected through the consent screen and Apple's tracking prompt. Showing non-personalized ads, frequency capping, fraud prevention and security: the legitimate interests of the developer of Quitline and the ad partners in funding a free app and keeping ads safe. Replying to your support email: our legitimate interest in helping you (or steps you ask for before a contract). Purchases: handled by Apple under Apple's terms.
  • Your rights. Access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection (including to processing based on legitimate interests), data portability, and withdrawing consent at any time without affecting earlier processing. Withdraw ad consent in Quitline Settings > Ad Privacy Choices; object or ask about anything else by emailing SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD.
  • Complaints. You can complain to your local data protection authority. We would appreciate the chance to fix things first.
  • International transfers. Ad partners may process data in the United States and other countries. They rely on safeguards such as the EU Standard Contractual Clauses and, where they are certified, the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework; see their policies above.

California and other US states (CCPA / CPRA and similar laws)

  • Categories collected in the last 12 months (by ad partners through the free version only): identifiers (IDFA with your permission, IDFV, SDK IDs, IP address); internet or other electronic network activity (ad impressions and taps); approximate geolocation derived from IP; device information. Inferences may be drawn by ad partners for personalized ads if you allow it. We do not collect sensitive personal information, and your in-app data is never shared with ad partners.
  • Sources and purposes. Collected directly from your device by the ad SDKs, for the advertising, measurement, security and fraud-prevention purposes described above.
  • "Sale" and "sharing". We do not sell personal information for money. Letting ad partners use identifiers for cross-context behavioral advertising may count as "selling" or "sharing" under California law. To opt out: choose "Ask App Not to Track", and/or open Quitline Settings > Ad Privacy Choices and opt out of sale/sharing, or email us. You can also buy Pro to remove ads entirely.
  • Your rights. To know/access, delete, correct, opt out of sale or sharing, and limit the use of sensitive personal information (we do not use any). We will not discriminate against you for using these rights; the free version stays the same whether or not you opt out. An authorized agent may make a request on your behalf with your written permission. Because we hold no account data, we may not be able to link ad-partner data to you; we will tell you which partner to contact and how.
  • Retention. See Data retention.
  • Minors. We do not knowingly sell or share the personal information of consumers under 16.

Residents of other US states with consumer privacy laws (for example Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, Texas and Oregon) have similar rights to access, delete, correct and opt out of targeted advertising. Use the same steps above or email us. If we decline a request, you can appeal by replying to our answer with "Appeal" in the subject line.

Children and teens

Quitline is meant for people aged 13 and older and is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 (or the minimum age in your country). If you believe a child has provided personal information to us, for example by email, contact us and we will delete it. If you are a teen, we encourage you to also talk to a trusted adult, doctor or helpline about quitting; resources are on our support page.

Security

Your data is protected by iOS app sandboxing and Data Protection encryption, and you can add Face ID or passcode lock in Quitline. Because we don't operate a server, there is no developer-held database of your journey that could be breached. Keep your device passcode, your Apple ID and any exported files secure.

Contact

Email SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD for questions, privacy requests or complaints. If you email us, we receive your email address and whatever you write, and use it only to reply; please don't include more health details than you need to. We aim to answer within 7 days, and privacy requests within the time the law requires (30 days under GDPR, 45 days under CCPA).

Changes and changelog

If we change how Quitline handles data, we will update this page and the date at the top before the change takes effect, and for significant changes we will tell you in the app. The App Store privacy label is kept in line with this page.
